name: Eye-area radiofrequency / Thermage eyes

card.summary: Radiofrequency heating of the eye area to tighten skin and soften wrinkles; one registered trial exists, results not reviewed here.
card.note: RF tightening has reported burns, dents and scarring in some patients.

quick.overview:
Radiofrequency (RF) skin tightening uses RF energy to heat the skin, with the aim of stimulating collagen and reducing fine lines and laxity. Thermage is a brand from Solta Medical, and the eye-area version targets wrinkles and looseness around the eyes.

Sources reviewed describe the technique in general and list one registered trial of an electrosurgical device for wrinkles around the eye corners; its results were not available for this article.
quick.mechanism: RF heats the dermis, with a target around 67 C described, to prompt remodeling of collagen and elastin. Penetration depth depends on electrode configuration (monopolar, bipolar or unipolar) [1].
quick.risks: Reported problems include pain severe enough to need sedation, skin dents from uneven healing, fat necrosis and atrophic scarring [1]. The eye area is delicate; no source reviewed describes eye-specific safety data.

lead: Eye-area radiofrequency treatment, often called Thermage eyes after the Thermage device brand, applies radiofrequency (RF) energy to the skin around the eyes to tighten loose skin, soften wrinkles and lift the brow slightly. It is marketed as a noninvasive alternative to surgery for people who want a firmer, less crepey eye area and a more open look without incisions or downtime [1].

RF skin tightening is described as heating the dermis to stimulate collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production [1]. Many manufacturers make such devices, including Solta Medical (Thermage), Venus Concept, Syneron, BTL and Lumenis [1].

A 2003 multicenter study of the original ThermaCool system, using single treatments around the eyes in 86 subjects, reported wrinkle score improvement in most blinded photo ratings and a measurable brow lift in many treated eyebrows [2].
infobox: At least 0.5 mm in 61.5% of eyebrows in a 2003 study [2]
2nd-degree burns 0.36% of applications in a 2003 study [2]

paras: RF devices use monopolar, bipolar or unipolar electrodes, which change how deep the energy penetrates [1]. Cited studies in the general literature include a blinded comparison of fractional RF with surgical facelift and studies showing new collagen and elastin formation, though several statements in the Wikipedia article carry citation-needed tags [1].
Wikipedia notes patients may report pain needing sedation, that improper application can leave dents from uneven healing, and that fat necrosis and atrophic scarring have been reported [1].

A 2003 multicenter study in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine treated 86 subjects once with the ThermaCool TC system and followed them for 6 months. Blinded photograph scoring showed a Fitzpatrick wrinkle score improvement of at least 1 point in 83.2 percent of treated periorbital areas, while treating physicians, without pre-treatment photographs, noted improvement in 28.9 percent. Half of subjects were satisfied or very satisfied with wrinkle reduction, and 61.5 percent of eyebrows were lifted by at least 0.5 mm. Edema and erythema were rare, second-degree burns occurred in 0.36 percent of applications (21 of 5,858), and three patients had small residual scars at 6 months [2].

A 2011 study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology treated six people with six sessions of monopolar RF at two-week intervals and measured histology: it reported noticeable clinical improvement with high satisfaction and objective changes in elastin and collagen in biopsies [3].

A registered single-blind, paired-design, non-inferiority device trial (n=80, completed, started 2024) assessed a universal electrosurgical device for temporary improvement of mild and moderate wrinkles around the eye corners and cheek folds [4]. No results were available for this entry.

timeline.event: Multicenter study reports periorbital tightening with ThermaCool RF [2]
Study documents collagen and elastin changes after RF sessions [3]
Registered trial of an electrosurgical device for eye-corner wrinkles begins [4]

angle.text: People have RF applied to the periorbital area to firm sagging upper and lower eyelid skin and lines at the eye corners without surgery. The treatment is performed in a clinic and results are described as developing over months.
